source.name: QGIS Training Manual
source.note: Paraphrased exercise goals and factual operation mappings; no private workbook material.

selection.ordering: sha256(seed:id) within step count; original 20 retain their split; new cases balanced within step count
selection.note: The original 20 case objects are unchanged. The other 73 use the reviewed QGIS Training Manual mapping; repeated operations are explicitly enabled per case.

cases.goal: Find the places that satisfy both conditions at once: less than 50 m from a road and within 1 km of a school.
cautions: The school criterion is direct-line distance, not travel distance by road.

cases.goal: Limit my study area to the districts of Bellville, Cape, Goodwood, Kuils River, Mitchells Plain, Simon Town and Wynberg.

inputs.role: administrative districts with a NAME_2 name field

cautions: District names must match the attribute values exactly (e.g. 'Simon Town', 'Kuils River'); listing the field's values avoids typos.
An IN list and a chain of OR comparisons are equivalent.

cases.goal: Of the candidate buildings (all larger than 100 square metres), which ones touch the land we found to be suitable terrain? Give me them as a new layer.

inputs.role: candidate buildings from the earlier vector analysis (over 100 m2)

cautions: An intersection cuts the buildings along the terrain boundary: the output geometries are pieces of buildings, not whole buildings.
Touching suitable terrain is not the same as lying on it.
cases.source_section: Try Yourself (combine buildings with suitable terrain)

cases.goal: Convert three shapefiles in a folder to ED50 / UTM zone 29N (EPSG:23029) in one go, each saved under a name derived from the input name.
cautions: Output filenames must differ per row; build them from the input layer name.

cases.goal: Are my random sample points clustered, evenly spread or randomly scattered? Give me the summary measure and its significance.
cautions: The result depends on the study area implied by the layer extent and on the CRS units of the distances.
cases.source_section: Follow Along: Nearest Neighbor Analysis (within layer)

cases.goal: Pick out the major roads from the road table in the database and put the result on the map as a layer named roads_primary.

inputs.role: lines table in the PostGIS database

cautions: A query result can only be loaded as a layer if you name a column with unique integer values and the geometry column
cases.source_section: Follow Along: Executing SQL Queries with DB Manager

cases.goal: From the elevations measured at 100 scattered points, build a continuous elevation surface to get an idea of the terrain, weighting nearby points strongly (power 5).
cautions: 100 sample points are too few for a detailed terrain surface: the result is only a general and potentially misleading picture.
The Z field must be set explicitly in the advanced parameters.

cases.goal: Remove the remaining duplication from the people data: split full names into first and last name, and move towns and countries into their own tables that each person refers to.

inputs.role: people table linked to a streets table

cases.goal: Remove Joe Smith from the people table.
Compute how steep the ground is everywhere, as a percentage gradient, from the 30 m elevation model.

inputs.role: aligned 30 m elevation model in UTM

cases.goal: Register Joe Smith, house number 55 on Main Street, phone 072 882 33 21, even though Main Street is not yet in the list of streets.
What is the shortest route along the road network between these two locations, and how long is it? (about 1000 m in the example)

inputs.role: start and end locations (picked on the map)

cases.goal: Change the saved people-per-street summary so its rows come out sorted by street name.
Which records of one table are missing from a second table with the same structure?

These aerial images are in latitude/longitude but the rest of my project uses a different coordinate system; give me copies already in the project's projection so I am not relying on on-the-fly display.

inputs.role: aerial image or virtual mosaic of tiles

cases.goal: We are in the Southern Hemisphere and want sunny plots, so map which compass direction each patch of ground faces (0 = north, 90 = east, 180 = south, 270 = west).
Make a shaded-relief image of the terrain from the 30 m elevation model to use as a backdrop.
Summarise the sampled elevations: count, sum, mean, median, standard deviation, min, max, range, quartiles and how many values are missing.
Create a streets table where each street gets an automatically numbered unique id and a name of up to 50 characters, then check its structure and contents.
Get the centre point of road 1 and of the Saskatchewan region as map layers.
Turn the 0-360 degree facing-direction map into four classes: 1 north (0-45 and 315-360), 2 east (45-135), 3 south (135-225), 4 west (225-315).

inputs.role: aspect in degrees derived from the dem

cautions: North spans the 0/360 wrap, so it needs two table rows mapping to the same class (5 rows for 4 classes).
How shared boundary values (45, 135, ...) are assigned depends on the 'Range boundaries' setting; check it.
Doing this with the raster calculator is possible but the expression becomes very long.

cases.goal: Give me the summary statistics (count, mean, min, max, spread and so on) of the year-2000 population field across all features of my layer.
Show me all the areas where the terrain is above 1000 metres.
The buyers want to build a house, so I need to know how steep the ground is everywhere in the study area, in degrees, cell by cell.
For each of my sample points, look up the terrain elevation from the SRTM elevation model and store it as an attribute.
Working in a GRASS database, map which direction each part of the terrain faces from the elevation model.
I want a world map of the oceans drawn on a circular Van der Grinten projection, which is not among the predefined coordinate systems, using a sphere of radius 6371000 m.
Save the count of people per street as a reusable virtual table I can query like any other table.
Work out which compass direction each part of the terrain faces, in degrees, from the 30 m elevation model.

inputs.role: aligned 30 m elevation model in UTM

cases.goal: From the zoning map, pull out the land zoned as rural into its own layer.

inputs.role: generalised zoning polygons with a Gen_Zoning field

cases.goal: Among the buildings that overlap suitable terrain, which ones only partly sit on it and should therefore be ruled out?
cautions: Buildings that were sliced by the intersection lie only partly on suitable terrain, so only part of the property is suitable; they should be eliminated.

cases.goal: Simplify the facing-direction map into just four categories, north = 1, east = 2, south = 3, west = 4, using a rules file.
cautions: Aspect runs 0 (north) through 90, 180, 270 to 360 (north again), so north needs rules on both ends of the range.
Read the tool's manual tab for the exact rule syntax.

cases.goal: Add a new street, for example 'Low Road', to the streets table.
My land-use polygons have no size attribute; add one with the area of each polygon so I can rank them by size.
Which of the settlements in my places layer are classified as towns?

inputs.role: places with a 'place' type attribute and a 'name'

cases.goal: Look up how the coordinate system WGS 84 (EPSG 4326) is defined inside my spatial database.
I have the 1994 inventory figures for each forest stand in a CSV keyed by stand number. Attach them to my digitized stand polygons and save the result as a new permanent stands file.

inputs.role: digitized forest stands with stand ID
1994 stand inventory table (CSV) with stand ID

cases.goal: Which regions share a border with Hokkaido? I expect Missouri, Saskatchewan, Wales and also Queensland.
Mark every east-facing cell (facing between 45 and 135 degrees) as 1 and everything else as 0.
Every time someone's phone number changes, automatically record the person's name and the time of the change in a log table.
From the polygonised terrain layer, give me a new layer containing only the areas marked as suitable (value 1).
My elevation model is in metres; give me the same surface in feet (multiply by 3.28084).
Tell me the basic facts about this elevation grid: its size in rows and columns, its range of values and where the file lives.
Mark every cell whose gradient is between 15% and 60% as suitable (1) and everything else as 0.
I have a layer with two land parcels and I need one representative point at the geometric centre of each parcel, saved as a new point layer.

Before I measure any distances, put all my town layers (buildings, roads, schools, restaurants, land use) into a metric UTM coordinate system suited to the region, in a new GeoPackage so the original data stays untouched.
Mark every cell that gets more than 1000 mm of rain per year as 1 and the rest as 0.
Give me the buildings that touch or fall inside the zone that is both near a road and near a school, as their own layer.
Keep only the candidate habitat patches larger than 6000 square metres.

inputs.role: candidate habitat polygons with an area field

cases.goal: The elevation grid looks flat and abstract; make a shaded-relief image of the terrain with the sun in the north-west (azimuth 300 degrees) at 40 degrees above the horizon, no vertical exaggeration.
Which people live within 2 degrees of the location longitude 33, latitude -34?
Find the parts of the terrain-suitable areas that also lie at least 250 m inside rural land.
List each person with their house number and the name of the street they live on, instead of the street's number.
My building footprints are in latitude/longitude; I need a copy of them in WGS 84 / UTM zone 34S (EPSG:32734) so that distances and areas come out in metres.
Get the first corner point of every area in the city boundary table.
Same question without an intermediate layer: which regions other than Hokkaido are less than 100 metres from it?
From the systematic sample plots, what is the average growing stock volume per hectare and the average number of stems per hectare for the whole forest?

inputs.role: sample plot results with volume (m3/ha) and stems per ha

cases.goal: Count the people living on each street, showing the street's name rather than its number.
How long is the boundary of the Queensland region, and how large is its area?
cautions: Results are in the units of the layer CRS (and squared units for area)

cases.goal: Show each person's name, the name of their street and their position written out as readable coordinates.
Of the houses already close to a road and a school, keep only those that are also within 500 m of a restaurant.
cautions: Restaurants must be in the projected (metric) layer, otherwise 500 is not metres.
cases.source_section: Try Yourself: Further Filter our Buildings

cases.goal: List, without repeats, the town names of all buildings that lie in the Queensland region.
Keep only the rural land that is at least 250 m in from the edge of the rural zone, as one merged area.
Who lives on street number 1?
List people with their house numbers sorted by house number, and then sorted by name and house number.

Keep only the candidate buildings that sit inside large continuous patches of suitable terrain, i.e. where suitable ground extends at least 100 m in every direction, and save them as the final answer.
cautions: A negative buffer distance shrinks the polygons (interior buffer); what remains is ground with suitable terrain for 100 m around it.
The distance is in metres only because the project uses a projected CRS; in a geographic CRS the same number would be degrees.

Selecting buildings that intersect the shrunken layer still keeps buildings that extend partly outside it; the manual accepts them because they lie within the original suitable terrain, so check containment against the original layer if 'entirely within' is the real requirement.
The 100 m threshold is a heuristic loosely tied to the 'over 100 m2' building size; the units (metres vs square metres) are not the same quantity.

cases.goal: Reduce the number of corner points on one of the joined land-use areas, choosing how much detail to give up.
Which buildings lie inside the KwaZulu region? Keep the answer as a layer I can show on the map.
cautions: A view loaded as a layer needs the gid key and the geometry column in its select list

cases.goal: Map the area that is within 1 km in a straight line of any school, merged into one zone, with smooth edges.
Work out the floor-plan area of each candidate house in square metres and keep only those of at least 100 m2.
cautions: The area is in square metres only because the layer is in a projected CRS in metres.
Edits made with the field calculator must be saved (toggle editing off) before filtering.
The manual's criterion says 'more than 100' but the filter uses >= 100: decide whether the boundary value is included.
cases.source_section: Follow Along: Select Buildings of the Right Size

cases.goal: Cut the elevation and rainfall grids down to the outline of my selected districts.

For the 1854 London cholera outbreak, divide the area into the zones closest to each water pump and total the number of deaths in each zone, where each point is a building with a death count attribute.

inputs.role: buildings with cholera deaths, COUNT field

cases.goal: How many attributes does each river record carry?
How many people are in the table, and how many live on each street?
Split the terrain into three elevation bands: up to 1000 m = 1, 1000 to 1400 m = 2, 1400 m to the highest point = 3.
Make lighter versions of the road lines with less detail, once with a tolerance of 20 and once with 50 map units.
Mark every cell whose ground faces roughly north (direction 270 to 90 degrees through 0) as 1 and everything else as 0, on the same grid as the aspect map.

inputs.role: aspect in degrees derived from the dem

cases.goal: List the street names, show every street record, and show only the record for Main Road.
From each of these points, which parts of the street network can be reached by travelling no more than 250 m along the roads?
Join a set of points, such as GPS waypoints, into a single line in the order of their id (or of their timestamp).

inputs.role: points layer with an ordering field

cases.goal: Where is the average location of my sample points, and how does it compare with the geometric centre of the study area they were drawn from?
Give me the elevation statistics (min, max, mean, etc.) inside one particular sub-basin of my watershed map.
cautions: The clip uses only the selected polygon; without a selection all polygons are used.

cases.goal: Cut the road lines down to the part that falls inside a clipping area, keeping the road attributes and dropping roads that end up empty.
Draw lines of equal value every 10 units on my interpolation-disagreement surface, using several engines.
Produce two yes/no maps from the terrain: one for ground with a gradient of at most 2 degrees, one for at most 5 degrees.

inputs.role: slope in degrees derived from the dem

cases.goal: Derive each city's boundary from where its residents live: the tightest outline without inward bends around all its addresses, widened by a margin, stored in a new table of areas.
cautions: The manual's answer stops at the convex hull and never applies the buffer it asks for
The answer replaces city_id with a row number, which matches the real city ids only if they are consecutive from 1
A city with fewer than three distinct addresses gives a point or line, which the polygon constraint rejects
In WGS 84 a buffer distance is in degrees

cases.goal: For each town name, draw the smallest outline without inward bends that encloses all buildings with that name, numbered in order of town name.
cautions: A group with fewer than three distinct points yields a point or a line, not a polygon

cases.goal: Find every region other than Hokkaido that comes within 100 metres of Hokkaido, so that small gaps or slivers in the borders do not hide a neighbour.
cautions: The 100 is in the layer CRS units; it means metres only because this data is projected
Hokkaido itself intersects its own zone and must be excluded

cases.goal: Show me all the land that lies within 50 m of a road, as a single merged zone rather than one overlapping strip per road.
Cut my elevation model into separate rasters, one per watershed polygon, so each contains only the elevations of its own watershed.
Turn the coordinate pair (1, 1) into a point, read it back as readable text, and get the area within 1 unit around it.
Show only people whose house number is below 50, sorted by house number; then find people whose name contains an 's', and those whose name contains an 'r' in any case.
Merge my municipalities into one shape per province (PROVINCIA attribute) with several engines and find the differences in geometry and attributes between the results.
